verdict_vs_market.quote: It's a solid offer, but it's below the typical pay for this level

verdict_vs_current.quote: Year 1: Google is about $75K ahead on the parts you can count on.

recommendation.quote: Don't accept it as is. Negotiate, mainly for more equity and a sign-on bonus, and only walk away if Google won't move.

equity_grounding.quote: Levels.fyi lists median total compensation at L6 as $605,720 per year for Google PMs in the Bay Area. That figure probably includes stacked refreshes from people who've been there a while, but your year-1 total of $552K is still below it.

uses_public_incumbent_benchmark.quote: Levels.fyi lists median total compensation at L6 as $605,720 per year for Google PMs in the Bay Area.

caveat_tenure_offering_company.quote: That figure probably includes stacked refreshes from people who've been there a while

refresh_valued_at.quote: Leave the recruiter's refresh example out of your comparison. Meta's refreshes stack over time too.

steady_state_math.quote: Year 5 and later: Google looks like roughly $235K + $47K + ~$250K in refreshes, about $530K. That's about what you make now.

uses_given_refresh_numbers.quote: Comparing Google's projected $458K in year 4 against your Meta pay today makes Google look better than it is.

walkaway_tied_to.quote: If they won't move at all, the offer is still better than staying for pay, just not by much. In that case, comp alone isn't a strong reason to leave a job you like.

unsupported_claims.claim: Google new-hire grants often vest front-loaded at 33/33/22/12 or 38/32
unsupported_claims.quote: One reported schedule is 33% / 33% / 22% / 12%, vesting monthly with no cliff, and others report 38% in the first year and 32% in the second.

unsupported_claims.claim: Google offers most increase from GSUs, then sign-on, then base
unsupported_claims.quote: According to negotiation guides, at Google you will typically get most of your increase from GSUs (Google Stock Units), followed by your sign-on bonus, and then your base salary.

missing_info_requested: exact timing of next Meta vest and bonus payout

ask_focus.quote: Negotiate, mainly for more equity and a sign-on bonus, and only walk away if Google won't move.

rsu_annualized.quote: The recruiter's $270K in year 1 assumes the grant vests evenly, 25% a year.

year1_vs_recurring.quote: A realistic result is roughly $630K–$660K in year 1, about $150K+ more than staying at Meta.

forfeiture_netted.quote: You described your Meta pay as $526K/yr, but what you'd actually get in the next 12 months is lower

forfeiture_as_loss.quote: You'd give up about $200K of Meta stock vesting in the next year, plus whatever vests after that. Some sources say a sign-on bonus at Google often fills the gap in year one compensation when your previous employer's unvested equity is being left behind.
